findings.title: Existing identity silently restarts as new
findings.scenario: Scenario 1: Existing identity silently restarts as new - EX-START
findings.summary: The scenario hypothesizes that a kvstore process with an existing replica identity can treat an unreadable or unparsable view file as first initialization. The cited startup path falls through to Replica::new and can overwrite the view file, while the library contract requires callers to recover an old identity with persisted view information before releasing outputs. The retained evidence says malformed and invalid-UTF-8 view files are accepted as view 0, and a public-API schedule can then commit different operations at slot 1 after this constructor choice. The model-checking source contains no findings, so this mechanism is retained as a code-review candidate for confirmation.

findings.title: Accepted self-quorum never triggers commit
findings.scenario: Scenario 2: Accepted self-quorum never triggers commit - LIB-SINGLE
findings.summary: The scenario hypothesizes that a one-member configuration is accepted and has quorum 1, but the request path never commits using the initial self acknowledgment. The cited normal-case code records the primary's own acknowledgment in on_request, while the commit evaluation is performed only when a peer PrepareOk arrives. The retained public-API observation leaves a fault-free singleton at op 1, commit 0, and no replies after repeated idle and retry rounds. The model-checking source contains no findings, so this mechanism is retained as a code-review candidate for confirmation.

findings.title: One blocked peer stalls all queued destinations
findings.scenario: Scenario 3: One blocked peer stalls all queued destinations - EX-WRITER
findings.summary: The scenario hypothesizes that the kvstore example's shared FIFO sender can let one non-reading or stalled peer delay traffic to otherwise healthy peers. The cited sender loop performs blocking write_all calls without a write timeout, and connect timeout only bounds connection establishment. The retained socket probe delayed healthy traffic for about 802 ms while the failure detector is based on 100 ms ticks and five missed periods. The model-checking source contains no findings, so this mechanism is retained as a code-review candidate for confirmation.

findings.title: View file rename is released without durable directory publication
findings.scenario: Scenario 4: View file rename is released without durable directory publication - EX-FSYNC
findings.summary: The scenario hypothesizes that persist_view treats a successful rename as durable publication of the new view-file name without syncing the parent directory. The cited path writes and syncs a temporary file, renames it, caches the view, and the event loop later releases outputs after persistence succeeds. Under a filesystem crash model that can lose an unsynced directory entry, a restart may observe an old or missing view despite messages having already been released. The model-checking source contains no findings, so this mechanism is retained as a code-review candidate for confirmation.

findings.title: Wall-clock recovery tokens lack guaranteed freshness
findings.scenario: Scenario 5: Wall-clock recovery tokens lack guaranteed freshness - EX-NONCE
findings.summary: The scenario hypothesizes that the kvstore example supplies a recovery nonce from wall-clock time even though Replica::recover requires a distinct nonce for every recovery. The cited example uses SystemTime nanoseconds narrowed to u64 with an error fallback of 0, while the library filters same-view stale recovery responses by the supplied nonce and quorum checks. This candidate is separate from the known client-id reuse issue and still requires confirmation of stale-response reachability through the example transport. The model-checking source contains no findings, so this mechanism is retained as a code-review candidate for confirmation.

findings.title: Test observers omit important state and transport histories
findings.scenario: Scenario 6: Test observers omit important state and transport histories - AS-01-AS-06, AS-LEAN
findings.summary: The scenario hypothesizes that simulator, DST, and retained Lean evidence can miss regressions because observers are incremental or batched and some environment assumptions are idealized. The cited areas include oracle checks that skip previously checked committed indices, whole-batch tick and delivery observation, replies outside the simulated fault network, reboot using saved in-memory state, singleton coverage gaps, a pre-healing liveness latch, and proof obligations with remaining assumptions. This is an assurance and test-gap candidate rather than a claimed conforming-library protocol counterexample, but the consolidator does not filter it out. The model-checking source contains no findings, so this mechanism is retained as a code-review candidate for confirmation.
